head: f4b61a475ee3032f45d8d29d098d122adbf7f337
scope: One combined NEW host-terrain reader/kernel, safe Rust/unsafe C bridge, Lua provider harness, conformance helper and original-fast-oracle source review. Closed a8 driver/census/cache/fixture review reused. Root additionally requested a bounded original a8 R1-R5 completion audit during this pass.
disposition: Changes requested:1 P1 and5 P2 grouped findings. No new backend/native/extraction acceptance. Original a8 bounded characterization/control evidence passes the checks stated below; it cannot clear these new-source defects.

findings.title: Remove the unmatched preprocessor terminator
findings.mechanism: The copied function declaration is followed by #endif without an open #if. build.rs unconditionally compiles this file, blocking every eech-world build. Root compile-only checkpoint subsequently confirmed exactly this error with actual exit1.
findings.bounded_correction: Remove the stray terminator, then build the actual affected target; retain the failed log. No numerical change is required.

findings.title: Validate non-wrapping and aligned geometry views before pointer formation
findings.mechanism: On the supported i686/size_t32 target, a u32 offset near UINT32_MAX plus the span can wrap and pass the addition-based length comparisons. The subsequent geometry+offset pointer and face/reference reads are outside the allocation. Independently, odd offsets for typed xz/word-reference arrays pass and produce unaligned typed C reads. Current Windows shipping is x86_64; this does not mean a malformed retail file has been observed.
findings.bounded_correction: Use off<=buffer_length and required<=buffer_length-off (checked products) for every view, and reject misaligned views or copy/decode to suitably aligned owned storage. Exercise boundary/overflow offsets and odd xz/word-reference offsets against production reader code, including32-bit semantics.

findings.title: Serialize the complete static C solver interval across independently created maps
findings.mechanism: The public safe Rust methods can be called on independently opened Terrain values in different threads. !Send on an individual raw-pointer value does not stop constructing one map per thread. C query/map/reference/diagnostic statics race, so one call can use the other allocation or stale pointers after its map drops. New conformance and forged-hint integration tests run concurrently by Cargo default and already expose this pattern. Documenting not thread safe does not make the safe Rust API sound.
findings.bounded_correction: Serialize every safe entry that uses these statics with one shared lock, or use thread-local/per-call C contexts. Cover concurrent independently loaded maps through real methods; preserve single-thread query arithmetic/order.

findings.title: Bind opaque hints to their issuing map and protect the cached normal
findings.mechanism: The e1 hex codec is not an issuance check. A structurally valid hint with finite normal[0,0,0] is accepted and copied directly into the find-fast record; if its triangle contains the point, line2197 computes0/0 instead of refusing. A hint from another map with coincident sector/face/reference/type fields also passes. This contradicts the documented forged/stale-hint contract and can corrupt physical answers while remaining in-bounds.
findings.bounded_correction: Use an opaque per-map issued-record token or equivalent verifiable map/record provenance, preserving legitimate cached normal bits rather than sanitizing the solver result. Refuse altered finite normals and cross-map stale hints; exercise actual provider/decoder/query paths.

findings.title: Restore bounded sweep counts and return only produced samples
findings.mechanism: The original fixture bounds count to200000; the new C sweep only checks count<0 and computes6+count first. count=INT_MAX wraps total negative under the configured-fwrapv and returns an empty successful report. Separately, Rust allocates and returns emit samples even if fewer than emit points exist: count0/emit256 returns6real samples plus250zero-initialized entries presented as samples.
findings.bounded_correction: Validate the original count range before computing total; size/truncate the result to min(emit,6+count), carrying the actual count explicitly if needed. Add small-count/large-emit and upper/overflow refusal cases against the production sweep.

findings.title: Require the intended terrain refusal and report completed frames honestly
findings.mechanism: missing/bad_* treats any dc.boot failure as an expected success and returns normally. bad_* similarly accepts any engine.frame failure, even if the malformed point callback never ran. An unrelated boot/map/frame failure therefore falsely greens the terrain contract. The summary currently emits requested frames after an early failure, which also overstates completed work.
findings.bounded_correction: Require mode-specific primary terrain-provider errors plus actual malformed-point trigger evidence; reject unrelated/setup/poison-only failures. Track completed frames and requested maximum separately. Preserve intentional RED on the unmoved DLL.

source_assessment.ownership: The backend owns its own map bytes and C solver outside the DLL. Production DLL dispatch is unchanged; no authority handoff is claimed yet. Public Lua point/fast/map answers and opaque hints carry values, not raw addresses or legacy entity heap IDs. Campaign terrain class/suitability/route policy stays core.
source_assessment.arithmetic: Read-only body comparison with6bbaa8197 terrelev.c found all8 triangle bodies equal after host-name/comment normalization. The query differs only by declared N1/N3 patches and host observation flags. Verified original Git file SHAef897d423c2d1a30bfec9cc9205c492a759020b5e0d85ee1d2a68d3df7311c9e. This is source comparison, not compiled bit equivalence. Fast interpolation expression/order matches terrsel.c; FE_TOWARDZERO setup/restoration is explicit but actual target conformance remains pending.
source_assessment.ffi: C/Rust DTO field order and repr(C) reviewed: Facts/Hint/RawAnswer/SweepReport/SweepSample correspond by inspection. No compiled C/Rust size/alignment/offset proof was executed or supplied here. Terrain retains Vec allocations until after C close; no buffer lifetime issue was identified apart from the shared-static concurrency defect.
source_assessment.new_fast_oracle: The original fast call is appended after the existing point operations at each sweep point, uses no game RNG or find-fast record, and is hashed separately. Existing point folds/order are retained by source inspection. Parser fast keys preserve hex strings. This new oracle has not compiled/run; original a8 traces contain no fast samples.
source_assessment.tests: Real-map integration tests compare raw sample bit strings, ordered hashes and counters, with explicit private-data SKIPPED behavior and FAST ORACLE ABSENT disclosure. They directly test the host kernel, not the public campaign-provider handoff. Existing hint tests omit modified finite normals/cross-map provenance. No tests were launched by reviewer.
compatibility_limits: Absent terrain.sim generation remains an explicit original behavior gap; must be resolved/dispositioned before full G1 acceptance.
Cuba/off-map, player/MP/save-restore and generic-host/native branches are not proven here.
Legacy loader/sector/tree/type-triangle/ground-impact and active device/subobject/target-point services remain D3 work, not D5 deferrals.
Cleared-shared-record conformance initialization differs from the original boot-left record; first-iteration/cache effects require actual comparison rather than an assumed equivalence.

BINF03f79c2e85777a9d047035d44ab5cc355c07b9afceb6076d8291d2720598e773. Verified current frozen a8 clean source; actual runtime remains a8, never relabelled f4.

Affected C/Rust/Lua bounds, concurrency, provenance, cardinality and refusal controls; actual compilation/layout checks after source corrections.
Fresh named corrected fixture and original fast samples, both-map conformance and actual public-provider RED before production handoff.
Then host dispatch/authority/refusal/default and final D3 completion gates under the finite scope; no baseline/tolerance changes.
